---
title: "4: Axioms of Probability"
---

The Kolmogorov axioms are the rules that every probability assignment must obey. They should be understood as consistency requirements rather than as formulas to memorize.

## **Axiom 1 — Nonnegativity**

$$P(A) ≥ 0$$

Probabilities cannot be negative.

## **Axiom 2 — Normalization**

$$P(Ω) = 1$$

The entire modeled sample space has probability one.

## **Axiom 3 — Additivity for disjoint events**

$$P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B) \text{ when } A∩B=∅$$

If events cannot occur together, their probabilities add. More generally, this extends to countably many mutually exclusive events.

Note that the axioms do not tell us what probability a physical experiment should have. They tell us what a consistent probability model must obey once its probabilities are specified.

### **Consequences we can derive from the Axioms**

::: practice-box
What is the probability of the empty set ($\emptyset$)?

<details>

<summary>Click to show answer</summary>

**Answer:** Because $Ω$ and $∅$ are disjoint and $Ω∪∅=Ω$, additivity gives $P(Ω)=P(Ω)+P(∅)$. Therefore $P(∅)=0$.

</details>
:::

::: practice-box
For some event $A$ in our space $\Omega$ what is the probability of the complement of $A$ ($A^c$)?

<details>

<summary>Click to show answer</summary>

**Answer:** $A$ and $Aᶜ$ partition $Ω$, so $P(Aᶜ)=1−P(A)$.

</details>
:::

## **Bounds and Monotonicity**

The axioms imply:

$$0 ≤ P(A) ≤ 1$$

Also, if $A⊆B$, then $P(A)≤P(B)$. A smaller event cannot contain more probability than the event containing it.

## **Inclusion–Exclusion Returns**

The inclusion–exclusion principle from counting carries directly into probability:

$$P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B)−P(A∩B)$$

This is not really a new formula. It is the same overlap correction already developed through Venn diagrams. Adding $P(A)$ and $P(B)$ counts the overlap twice; subtracting it once leaves one copy.
